name: XT60 (high-current DC)
ascii:
.-------------.
       /  (+)     (-)  \     XT60 -- high-current DC (RC / LiPo / DIY)
      /                 \      (+) and (-) are molded into the housing
      '-----------------'      chamfered corners key the polarity
        ~60 A continuous  (XT30 = smaller, XT90 = bigger)
description: The yellow polarized bullet connector for high-current DC -- LiPo batteries, RC/drones, e-bikes, and DIY power. Two large gold bullet contacts (+ and -) in a nylon housing rated around 60 A continuous. The housing's chamfered corners and molded +/- markings key the polarity so it can only fully seat one way.

contacts.name: POSITIVE
contacts.description: positive terminal (molded '+' on the housing). The bullet is often the female socket on the battery side

variants: XT30 (~30 A) is the smaller sibling, XT90 (~90 A) the bigger; same idea, not intermateable. XT90-S is an anti-spark version with a pre-charge resistor.
There's no signal here -- it's pure DC power. Balance/telemetry leads (JST-XH etc.) are separate connectors on a LiPo pack.
gotchas: Connecting a charged LiPo through an XT60 arcs -- a visible spark on contact is normal for small packs. For big packs the inrush pits the contacts and stresses ESCs; that's what anti-spark (XT90-S) or a pre-charge resistor is for.
Polarity: the housing is keyed so you can't FULLY reverse it, but a careless half-insert can still bridge the wrong way -- match the molded + / - before pushing.
Soldering the bullets needs a lot of heat (they're big brass); a cold joint on a 60 A connector overheats under load. Tin both, heat the cup, flow the wire, and don't bridge + to -.
Rated ~60 A continuous but that assumes good solder joints and airflow; sustained max current gets the contacts hot.
notes: XT60 2-contact polarized high-current DC connector (+/-), ~60 A. XT30/XT90 siblings + anti-spark XT90-S noted. RC/LiPo standard.
